symbols.name: \(K\)
symbols.def: \(K\) is the fixed cross-fitting fold count.

symbols.name: \(\bar d\)
symbols.def: \(\bar d\) is the directional rarity cap.

symbols.name: \(t\)
symbols.def: \(t\) is a null value for a directional probability of causation.

symbols.name: \(\Theta_{\mathrm{PN}},\Theta_{\mathrm{PS}},\mathfrak T\)
symbols.def: The functionals are given in \texttt{def:functionals}; \(\mathfrak T(x,a,y)=(x,1-a,1-y)\).

symbols.name: \(\psi_{t,n}^{\mathrm{PN}},\psi_{t,n}^{\mathrm{PS}},\eta_n^{\mathrm{PN}},\eta_n^{\mathrm{PS}}\)
symbols.def: The PN score and its transformed PS analogue are given in \texttt{def:scores}; \(\eta_n^{\mathrm{PN}}=(e_n,m_{0,n})\) and \(\eta_n^{\mathrm{PS}}=(1-e_n,1-m_{1,n})\).

symbols.name: \(s_j,a_{j,n},I_{k,n},\widehat e_{-k,n},\widehat m_{a,-k,n}\)
symbols.space: positive sequences, index sets, and functions
symbols.def: \(s_j=\beta_j/(2\beta_j+p)\), \(a_{j,n}=(\log n/n)^{s_j}\), \(I_{k,n}\) are deterministic balanced folds, and the fitted functions are defined in \texttt{def:crossfit}.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal B_n,\mathcal M_n^d(r),\mathcal M_{G,n}^d(r)\)
symbols.def: The monotone base class, rarity shells, and Gaussian sub-shells are defined in \texttt{def:classes}.

symbols.name: \(t_d,\widehat g_d,\widehat d_d,\sigma_d^2,\widehat\sigma_d^2,\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{score},d}\)
symbols.def: The directional score statistics and inversions are defined in \texttt{def:score-inversion}.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal X_J,\Xi_J^d,Q_\xi^d,S^{\mathrm{fin},d},d^d(\xi),H_t^d,\ell_\xi^d,\Lambda_J^d,p_t^{d,\mathrm{LF}},\mathcal C_{J,n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{fin},d},U_n\)
symbols.space: finite support, compact profiles, laws, statistics, and sets
symbols.def: The separate PN and PS finite profile experiments are defined in \texttt{def:finite-tests}; \(U_n\sim\operatorname{Unif}(0,1)\) is independent.

symbols.name: \(\mathsf N_n,\lambda,\nu_{\xi,c}^d\)
symbols.space: a Polish mark space and finite measures
symbols.def: The qualified marked-Poisson objects are defined in \texttt{def:marked-poisson}.

symbols.name: \(s_n,P_{n,h},\Delta_n,D_n,h,c_\alpha\)
symbols.def: The PN induced paths and lower-bound notation are defined in \texttt{def:induced-paths} and \texttt{def:least-favorable}.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal G_n,\Gamma_n^d,H_{n,t}^{\mathrm{cont},d},\Lambda_n^{\mathrm{cont},d},p_{n,t}^{\mathrm{cont},d},\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{cont},d}\)
symbols.type: pilot sigma-field, sieve objects, and random sets
symbols.def: The pilot-selected continuous profiling objects are defined in \texttt{def:continuous-lr-handle}.

novel.justification: The cap leaves every vanishing effective-count sequence admissible and makes the displayed monotone least-favorable type probabilities nonnegative.
Interior rare-event laws have information proportional to their factual probability; the condition excludes deterministic directional endpoints from the Gaussian sub-shell.
The PS direction has a distinct factual event and its own interior information condition.

definitions.name: Hölder ball
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal H^\beta(L)=\{g:[0,1]^p\to\mathbb R:\max_{|s|\le\lfloor\beta\rfloor}\lVert D^s g\rVert_\infty+\max_{|s|=\lfloor\beta\rfloor}\sup_{x\ne x'}|D^s g(x)-D^s g(x')|/\lVert x-x'\rVert^{\beta-\lfloor\beta\rfloor}\le L\}\).

definitions.name: identified PN and PS functionals
definitions.construction: \(\Theta_{\mathrm{PN}}(P_n)=1-E_{P_n}[e_n(X)m_{0,n}(X)]/E_{P_n}[e_n(X)m_{1,n}(X)]\) and \(\Theta_{\mathrm{PS}}(P_n)=1-E_{P_n}[(1-e_n(X))(1-m_{1,n}(X))]/E_{P_n}[(1-e_n(X))(1-m_{0,n}(X))]\), whenever their respective denominators are positive.

definitions.name: fixed-fold clipped spline learners
definitions.construction: For \(j\in\{e,0,1\}\), take tensor-product B-spline degree \(r_j\ge\lceil\beta_j\rceil\), \(K_{j,n}\asymp(n/\log n)^{1/(2\beta_j+p)}\) quasi-uniform interior knots per coordinate, and \(J_{j,n}=(K_{j,n}+r_j+1)^p\). On each training complement, fit \(e_n\) by logistic loss, fit \(m_{0,n}\) by \(\sum_{i\notin I_{k,n}}(1-A_i)\{Y_i-B_{0,n}(X_i)^\top\gamma\}^2\), and fit \(m_{1,n}\) by \(\sum_{i\notin I_{k,n}}A_i\{Y_i-B_{1,n}(X_i)^\top\delta\}^2\), over deterministic compact coefficient boxes containing Hölder approximants; clip to \([\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\), \([0,1]\), and \([0,1]\).

definitions.name: base, rarity, and Gaussian directional shells
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal B_n=\{P_n:\exists\widetilde P_n\text{ satisfying }\texttt{ass:consistency},\texttt{ass:conditional-exchangeability},\texttt{ass:monotonicity},\text{ whose observed projection satisfies }\texttt{ass:overlap},\texttt{ass:covariate-design},\texttt{ass:holder-propensity},\texttt{ass:holder-control},\texttt{ass:holder-treated}\}\). For \(r\in(0,\bar d]\), \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{PN}}(r)=\{P\in\mathcal B_n:E_P[AY]=r\}\) and \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{PS}}(r)=\{P\in\mathcal B_n:E_P[(1-A)(1-Y)]=r\}\). If \(nr\to\infty\), \(\mathcal M_{G,n}^{\mathrm{PN}}(r)=\{P\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{PN}}(r):r\gg\max(a_{0,n}^2,na_{e,n}^2a_{0,n}^2)\text{ and }\texttt{ass:pn-score-information}\text{ holds}\}\); \(\mathcal M_{G,n}^{\mathrm{PS}}(r)=\{P\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{PS}}(r):r\gg\max(a_{1,n}^2,na_{e,n}^2a_{1,n}^2)\text{ and }\texttt{ass:ps-score-information}\text{ holds}\}\).

definitions.name: separate abstract randomized finite profile tests
definitions.construction: Fix \(\mathcal X_J=\{x_1,\ldots,x_J\}\). For PN, \(\xi=(w,\beta,\gamma,u)\in\Xi_J^{\mathrm{PN}}\) has \(w\in\Delta_J\), clipped \(e_\beta\), clipped \(m_{0,\gamma}\), \(m_{0,\gamma}(x_i)\le u_i\le1\), and cells \(q_{i,11}=e_\beta(x_i)u_i\), \(q_{i,10}=e_\beta(x_i)(1-u_i)\), \(q_{i,01}=(1-e_\beta(x_i))m_{0,\gamma}(x_i)\), \(q_{i,00}=(1-e_\beta(x_i))(1-m_{0,\gamma}(x_i))\). For PS, the separate profile \(\xi=(w,\beta^{\mathrm{PS}},\gamma^{\mathrm{PS}},u^{\mathrm{PS}})\in\Xi_J^{\mathrm{PS}}\) has its own compact boxes, \(r_i=e_{\beta^{\mathrm{PS}}}^{\mathrm{PS}}(x_i)\), \(v_i=m_{0,\gamma^{\mathrm{PS}}}^{\mathrm{PS}}(x_i)\), \(v_i\le u_i^{\mathrm{PS}}\le1\), and cells \(q_{i,11}=r_iu_i^{\mathrm{PS}}\), \(q_{i,10}=r_i(1-u_i^{\mathrm{PS}})\), \(q_{i,01}=(1-r_i)v_i\), \(q_{i,00}=(1-r_i)(1-v_i)\). For direction \(d\), \(Q_\xi^d(L=i,C=c)=w_iq_{i,c}^d\), \(S^{\mathrm{fin},d}\sim(Q_\xi^d)^{\otimes n}\), and \(d^d(\xi)=\sum_iw_iq_{i,11}^d\in[0,\bar d]\). Let \(G_{J,+}^d=\{(t,\xi):d^d(\xi)>0,\sum_iw_i r_i^d[(1-t)u_i^d-v_i^d]=0\}\), where \(r_i^{\mathrm{PN}}=e_\beta(x_i)\), \(v_i^{\mathrm{PN}}=m_{0,\gamma}(x_i)\), and \(u_i^{\mathrm{PN}}=u_i\). Put \(\overline G_J^d=\operatorname{cl}(G_{J,+}^d)\) in \([0,1]\times\Xi_J^d\), \(H_t^d=\{\xi:(t,\xi)\in\overline G_J^d\}\), \(\ell_\xi^d(s)=\sum_j\log\{w_{L_j}q_{L_j,C_j}^d\}\), and \(\Lambda_J^d(t;s)=2[\sup_{\Xi_J^d}\ell_\xi^d(s)-\sup_{H_t^d}\ell_\xi^d(s)]\), with \(\log0=-\infty\). For \(\xi\in H_t^d\), \(p_{\xi,t}^d(s,u)=(Q_\xi^d)^{\otimes n}\{\Lambda_J^d(t;S)>\Lambda_J^d(t;s)\}+u(Q_\xi^d)^{\otimes n}\{\Lambda_J^d(t;S)=\Lambda_J^d(t;s)\}\), \(p_t^{d,\mathrm{LF}}=\sup_{\xi\in H_t^d}p_{\xi,t}^d\), and \(\mathcal C_{J,n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{fin},d}=\{t:p_t^{d,\mathrm{LF}}(S^{\mathrm{fin},d},U_n)>\alpha\}\), overridden by \([0,1]\) if the directional \(11\)-count is zero. The finite sample space makes each tail probability a finite polynomial; compactness, the closed graph, and a lexicographic maximizer make the maps Borel. Denominator-zero closure points have no directional target value.

definitions.name: qualified marked-Poisson finite limit
definitions.construction: For a specified compact directional profile family, a Polish mark space \(\mathcal E\), and finite rare-cell set \(\mathcal R\), define \(\mathsf N_n=\sum_{j=1}^n1\{C_j\in\mathcal R\}\delta_{(C_j,M_{j,n}^\circ)}\). Require \(nd_n^d\to\lambda\in[0,\infty)\), uniform convergence on continuity sets of the rare-cell mark measures divided by \(d_n^d\) to finite \(\nu_{\xi,c}^d\), tight total masses, unit normalized true directional \(11\)-mass, and a uniform \(o_P(1)\) common-cell log-likelihood remainder relative to the Poisson compensator. Then \(\mathsf N_n\Rightarrow\operatorname{PRM}(\lambda\sum_{c\in\mathcal R}\nu_{\xi,c}^d)\). Pilot- or fold-dependent marks require conditional convergence in probability and stable unconditioning. At \(\lambda=0\), the process is empty and the report is \([0,1]\).

definitions.name: capped monotone least-favorable construction
definitions.construction: For \(t\in[1/4,3/4]\) and \(d\in(0,\bar d]\), take \(X\sim\operatorname{Unif}([0,1]^p)\), \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) independently, and set \(P[(Y(0),Y(1))=(1,1)\mid X]=2(1-t)d\), \(P[(Y(0),Y(1))=(0,1)\mid X]=2td\), and \(P[(Y(0),Y(1))=(0,0)\mid X]=1-2d\). Its observed PN cells are \((d,(1-t)d,1/2-d,1/2-(1-t)d)\); the PS construction is the treatment-and-outcome swap.

definitions.name: real-data directional score inversions
definitions.construction: For \(d\in\{\mathrm{PN},\mathrm{PS}\}\), set \(t_d=\Theta_d(P_n)\), \(\widehat g_d(t)=n^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{i\in I_{k,n}}\psi_{t,n}^d(O_{i,n};\widehat\eta_{d,-k,n})\), \(\widehat\sigma_d^2(t)=\mathbb P_n[\{\psi_{t,n}^d(O_i;\widehat\eta_{d,-k(i),n})-\widehat g_d(t)\}^2]\), and \(\widehat d_{\mathrm{PN}}=\mathbb P_n(AY)\), \(\widehat d_{\mathrm{PS}}=\mathbb P_n[(1-A)(1-Y)]\). Define \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{score},d}=\{t\in[0,1]:\sqrt n|\widehat g_d(t)|/\widehat\sigma_d(t)\le z_{1-\alpha/2}\}\), with report \([0,1]\) for zero denominator or variance.

definitions.name: induced PN local experiments
definitions.construction: At an interior \(P_n\), set \(s_n(O)=d_n^{\mathrm{PN}}\psi_{t_{\mathrm{PN}},n}^{\mathrm{PN}}(O;\eta_n^{\mathrm{PN}})/\sigma_{\mathrm{PN}}^2\) and \(dP_{n,r}/dP_n(O)=\exp\{rs_n(O)-\kappa_n(r)\}\), restricted to dominated paths that remain in the class and admit a monotone full-data extension. Re-index so \(\Theta_{\mathrm{PN}}(P_{n,h})=t_{\mathrm{PN}}+h/\sqrt{nd_n^{\mathrm{PN}}}+o((nd_n^{\mathrm{PN}})^{-1/2})\), and define \(\Delta_n=(nd_n^{\mathrm{PN}})^{-1/2}\sum_i\psi_{t_{\mathrm{PN}},n}^{\mathrm{PN}}(O_{i,n};\eta_n^{\mathrm{PN}})\).

definitions.name: pilot-selected continuous profile-LR handle
definitions.construction: Conditional on an independent pilot sigma-field \(\mathcal G_n\), choose deterministic compact directional sieve families of continuous densities \(q_\gamma^d(x,a,y)=f_\rho(x)q_{\eta,d}(a,y\mid x)\), with directional monotonicity restrictions and positive-denominator closed nulls \(H_{n,t}^{\mathrm{cont},d}(\mathcal G_n)\subset\Gamma_n^d(\mathcal G_n)\). On an independent main sample set \(\ell_n^{\mathrm{cont},d}(\gamma)=\sum_i\log q_\gamma^d(O_i)\), \(\Lambda_n^{\mathrm{cont},d}=2[\sup_{\Gamma_n^d}\ell_n^{\mathrm{cont},d}-\sup_{H_{n,t}^{\mathrm{cont},d}}\ell_n^{\mathrm{cont},d}]\), \(p_{n,t}^{\mathrm{cont},d}(z,u\mid\mathcal G_n)=\sup_{\gamma\in H_{n,t}^{\mathrm{cont},d}}[P_\gamma^{\otimes n}[\Lambda_n^{\mathrm{cont},d}(t;Z)>\Lambda_n^{\mathrm{cont},d}(t;z)\mid\mathcal G_n]+uP_\gamma^{\otimes n}[\Lambda_n^{\mathrm{cont},d}(t;Z)=\Lambda_n^{\mathrm{cont},d}(t;z)\mid\mathcal G_n]]\), and \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{cont},d}=\{t:p_{n,t}^{\mathrm{cont},d}>\alpha\}\), with the directional zero-count report. The handle is to prove compactness, Borel calibration, and target approximation; it asserts no coverage for a nonsieve continuous law.

sampling_model.design: For each row, \(Z_n\sim P_n^{\otimes n}\), where \(P_n\) is the observed projection of an admitted full-data law.
sampling_model.units: Each unit provides \(X\), binary \(A\), and binary \(Y\).
sampling_model.treatment: Consistency, conditional exchangeability, monotonicity, and overlap identify directional PN and PS ratios.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Fixed-fold clipped spline ERM fits \(e_n\) by logistic loss, \(m_{0,n}\) on controls, and \(m_{1,n}\) on treated observations.

statements.statement: Under consistency, conditional exchangeability, monotonicity, and overlap, positive directional denominators imply \(\theta=\Theta_{\mathrm{PN}}(P_n)\) and \(\vartheta=\Theta_{\mathrm{PS}}(P_n)\). Both targets are invariant across admitted full-data extensions with common observed marginal, and \(E_{P_n}[\psi_{\Theta_{\mathrm{PN}}(P_n),n}^{\mathrm{PN}}(O;\eta_n^{\mathrm{PN}})]=0\).
statements.justification: It converts cross-world attribution targets into observed-law functionals.
statements.gap: Tian and Wu (2025) provide the regular identification benchmark, not directional rare-event shells.
statements.consumer: It licenses the PN/FAR target in Hannart and Naveau (2018) and the PS target in Tian and Wu's stroke application.

statements.statement: Under row-wise sampling, overlap, bounded design density, propensity Hölder regularity, and control Hölder regularity, the PN fits satisfy \(\max_k(\lVert\widehat e_{-k,n}-e_n\rVert_{2,P_n}\vee\lVert\widehat e_{-k,n}-e_n\rVert_\infty)=O_{P_n^{\otimes n}}(a_{e,n})\) and \(\max_k\lVert\widehat m_{0,-k,n}-m_{0,n}\rVert_{2,P_n}=O_{P_n^{\otimes n}}(a_{0,n})\). With held-out errors \(\delta_e,\delta_0\), its conditional bias is \(E[\delta_e(X)\delta_0(X)/\{1-\widehat e(X)\}\mid\widehat e,\widehat m_0]\), its conditional variance is \(\lesssim a_{0,n}^2+a_{e,n}^2E[m_{0,n}(X)]\), and its score difference is uniformly \(O_{P_n^{\otimes n}}(a_{0,n}/\sqrt n+a_{e,n}\sqrt{E[m_{0,n}(X)]/n}+a_{e,n}a_{0,n})\) in \(t\).
statements.justification: It derives the generic score error without monotonicity.
statements.gap: Regular DML does not expose the rare-scale control-regression term.
statements.consumer: It supplies the monotone PN specialization.

statements.statement: Under row-wise sampling, overlap, bounded design density, propensity Hölder regularity, and treated-regression Hölder regularity, the transformed-control PS fit has \(\max_k\lVert(1-\widehat m_{1,-k,n})-(1-m_{1,n})\rVert_{2,P_n}=O_{P_n^{\otimes n}}(a_{1,n})\), with the exact analogue of \texttt{lem:learning} after \(m_0\) is replaced by \(1-m_1\).
statements.justification: PS requires a distinct learned transformed-control regression.
statements.gap: A PN learning result is not closed under the treatment-and-outcome swap.
statements.consumer: It supplies the PS score theorem.

statements.statement: Under the causal assumptions and \texttt{lem:learning}, \(m_{0,n}(x)\le m_{1,n}(x)\) and \(E[m_{0,n}(X)]\le E[m_{1,n}(X)]\le d_n^{\mathrm{PN}}/\varepsilon\). Hence the PN score difference is \(O_{P_n^{\otimes n}}(a_{0,n}/\sqrt n+a_{e,n}\sqrt{d_n^{\mathrm{PN}}/n}+a_{e,n}a_{0,n})\), which is \(o_{P_n^{\otimes n}}(\sqrt{d_n^{\mathrm{PN}}/n})\) on \(\mathcal M_{G,n}^{\mathrm{PN}}(d_n^{\mathrm{PN}})\).
statements.justification: Monotonicity supplies the rare second-moment localization only after generic learning is established.
statements.gap: Neither regular DML nor fixed-law PN theory records this directional localization.
statements.consumer: It permits Gaussian PN intervals when rare factual counts diverge.

statements.statement: Under the causal assumptions and \texttt{lem:swapped-learning}, \(1-m_{1,n}(x)\le1-m_{0,n}(x)\) and \(E[1-m_{1,n}(X)]\le E[1-m_{0,n}(X)]\le d_n^{\mathrm{PS}}/\varepsilon\). The PS score difference is rare-scale negligible on \(\mathcal M_{G,n}^{\mathrm{PS}}(d_n^{\mathrm{PS}})\).
statements.justification: The PS direction has its own localization and learning threshold.
statements.gap: PN rarity neither implies PS positivity nor a treated-regression rate.

statements.statement: On each Gaussian sub-shell and separately by direction, held-out score errors obey \(\mathbb P_n\Delta_{\mathrm{PN}}^2=O_P(a_{0,n}^2+d_na_{e,n}^2)=o_P(d_n)\) and \(\mathbb P_n\Delta_{\mathrm{PS}}^2=O_P(a_{1,n}^2+d_na_{e,n}^2)=o_P(d_n)\). The centered variance decomposition, bounded scores, and \(nd_n\to\infty\) then yield \(\widehat\sigma_d^2(t_d)/\sigma_d^2\to_{P_n^{\otimes n}}1\) uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{G,n}^d(d_n)\).
statements.justification: Studentization is derived from primitive spline rates rather than assumed.
statements.gap: Regular PN inference does not give rare-shell empirical-variance control.
statements.consumer: It validates the Wald critical value in both score inversions.

statements.statement: For the construction in \texttt{def:least-favorable}, \(c_X\le1\le C_X\), \(\varepsilon\le1/2\le1-\varepsilon\), \(0<d\le\bar d\le1/2\), and Hölder radii containing constants certify structural membership. Its PN variance ratio equals \((1-t)\{2-t-4(1-t)d\}\), which lies in \([3/16,21/16]\) for \(t\in[1/4,3/4]\); the swapped PS ratio is identical. Thus \(t_\pm=1/2\pm h(nd)^{-1/2}\) belong to the corresponding Gaussian sub-shell for Gaussian schedules, and their product Kullback--Leibler divergence is bounded by a constant times \(h^2\).
statements.justification: It verifies that the same lower alternatives occupy the upper theorem's Gaussian domain.
statements.gap: Generic ratio lower bounds do not certify monotonicity, Hölder membership, and score information together.
statements.consumer: It creates a matching lower corollary for each Gaussian score theorem.

statements.statement: For every \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\), direction \(d\in\{\mathrm{PN},\mathrm{PS}\}\), and positive-denominator \(\xi_0\in G_{J,+}^d(t)\), \(((Q_{\xi_0}^d)^{\otimes n}\otimes\operatorname{Unif})\{t\in\mathcal C_{J,n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{fin},d}\}\ge1-\alpha\), because \(p_t^{d,\mathrm{LF}}\ge p_{\xi_0,t}^d\). The zero directional \(11\)-count reports \([0,1]\). Under every premise in \texttt{def:marked-poisson}, the corresponding finite LR experiment has the stated marked-Poisson limit.
statements.justification: It gives both directions fully defined, measurable discrete randomized calibration.
statements.gap: Huwang (1995) diagnoses normal-binomial failure and McGrath and Burke (2024) compare rare-binomial intervals; neither supplies causal composite-null profiles.
statements.consumer: It tells Hannart and Naveau climate PN/FAR analyses when sparse factual counts demand discrete calibration and nonshrinking intervals.

statements.statement: For any deterministic schedule \(d_n\) with \(nd_n\to\infty\), uniformly over \(P_n\in\mathcal M_{G,n}^{\mathrm{PN}}(d_n)\), \(\widehat g_{\mathrm{PN}}(t_{\mathrm{PN}})=n^{-1}\sum_i\psi_{t_{\mathrm{PN}},n}^{\mathrm{PN}}(O_{i,n};\eta_n^{\mathrm{PN}})+o_{P_n^{\otimes n}}(\sqrt{d_n/n})\), \(\sqrt n\widehat g_{\mathrm{PN}}(t_{\mathrm{PN}})/\widehat\sigma_{\mathrm{PN}}(t_{\mathrm{PN}})\Rightarrow N(0,1)\), and \(\liminf_n\inf_{P_n\in\mathcal M_{G,n}^{\mathrm{PN}}(d_n)}P_n^{\otimes n}[t_{\mathrm{PN}}\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{score},\mathrm{PN}}]\ge1-\alpha\). Since \(\widehat g_{\mathrm{PN}}(t_{\mathrm{PN}}+u)-\widehat g_{\mathrm{PN}}(t_{\mathrm{PN}})=-u\widehat d_{\mathrm{PN}}\), bounded score variance and factual-count concentration imply \(\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_{G,n}^{\mathrm{PN}}(d_n)}E_{P_n^{\otimes n}}[\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{score},\mathrm{PN}})]=O((nd_n)^{-1/2})\).
statements.justification: It is a derived continuous-data Gaussian PN upper theorem on its stated sub-shell.
statements.gap: Tian and Wu (2025) treat regular semiparametric PN inference, not rare triangular shells or effective-count diameter.
statements.consumer: It yields a continuous PN interval for rare-event climate attribution when the Gaussian sub-shell applies.

statements.statement: For any deterministic schedule \(d_n\) with \(nd_n\to\infty\), uniformly over \(P_n\in\mathcal M_{G,n}^{\mathrm{PS}}(d_n)\), the transformed PS score inversion has asymptotic coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) under \(P_n^{\otimes n}\) and expected diameter \(O((nd_n)^{-1/2})\), derived by the swapped rare-scale remainder, derived empirical variance consistency, and affine factual-frequency geometry.
statements.justification: It is a separate PS theorem rather than an inference from PN positivity.
statements.gap: Tian and Wu's regular PS benchmark does not impose the direction-specific rare learning regime.
statements.consumer: It supports the PS component of the Tian--Wu stroke-attribution application when the PS factual event is positive and sufficiently frequent.

statements.statement: Along the dominated, class-preserving PN paths in \texttt{def:induced-paths}, for bounded \(h\), \(\log[dP_{n,h}^{\otimes n}/dP_n^{\otimes n}]=h\Delta_n/v_n-h^2/(2v_n)+o_{P_n^{\otimes n}}(1)\), where \(v_n=\sigma_{\mathrm{PN}}^2/d_n^{\mathrm{PN}}\to v\in[c_G,C_G]\) and \(\Delta_n\Rightarrow N(0,v)\). Thus these induced local experiments are LAN with information \(1/v\).
statements.justification: LAN belongs to class-preserving likelihood paths, not to a confidence-set map.
statements.gap: A fixed-law efficiency calculation does not establish rare triangular LAN.
statements.consumer: It gives local-power interpretation to the PN score interval.

statements.statement: For every deterministic \(d_n\in(0,\bar d]\), every measurable PN set \(D_n\) with \(\liminf_n\inf_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{PN}}(d_n)}P_n^{\otimes n}[\Theta_{\mathrm{PN}}(P_n)\in D_n]\ge1-\alpha\) satisfies \(\liminf_n\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{PN}}(d_n)}E_{P_n^{\otimes n}}[\operatorname{diam}(D_n)]/\min\{1,(nd_n)^{-1/2}\}\ge c_\alpha\). The swapped PS statement holds on \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{PS}}(d_n)\). Consequently \(nd_n\to\lambda<\infty\) forces nonshrinking expected diameter. Restricting to \(\mathcal M_{G,n}^d(d_n)\) gives the matching Gaussian-sub-shell corollary.
statements.justification: It is the causal shellwise effective-count converse.
statements.gap: Gleser and Hwang (1987) supply a ratio-impossibility template, not the bounded monotone PN/PS reduction.
statements.consumer: It distinguishes unavoidable finite information from failure of a particular interval construction in rare climate attribution.

statements.statement: Can an independent pilot construct compact continuous directional sieve families, positive-denominator closed nulls, Borel least-favourable conditional calibration, and target approximation for the explicit \(\Lambda_n^{\mathrm{cont},d}\) and \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{cont},d}\) in \texttt{def:continuous-lr-handle}?
statements.justification: A continuous random-covariate profile LR must exist before it can be approximated by a finite profile.
statements.gap: Mikusheva and Sun (2022) invert jackknife Anderson--Rubin tests in many-weak linear IV, not pilot-selected causal PN/PS profile likelihoods.
statements.consumer: It is the construction needed for selected-threshold climate-attribution inference.

statements.statement: After \texttt{oeq:continuous-lr-construction} is resolved, can a pilot-selected finite profile approximate the displayed continuous LR and calibration at the target and bounded local alternatives, with stable conditional unconditioning and uniform integrability of \(\sqrt{nd_n^d}\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{cont},d})\)?
statements.justification: Finite exactness does not transfer automatically to a continuous random-\(X\) law.
statements.gap: No verified comparator couples rare causal profile LR calibration to continuous Hölder random-covariate laws.
statements.consumer: A solution would test whether the finite discrete procedure can supply an all-regime continuous likelihood-ratio frontier.

statements.statement: Can simultaneous directional continuous profiles remain honest after a climate threshold or projection is selected to maximize causal evidence?
statements.justification: Selection changes both the attribution target and the effective count.
statements.gap: Hannart and Naveau (2018) and Kiriliouk and Naveau (2020) optimize attribution evidence without selection-honest rare-score profiling.
statements.consumer: It would deliver uncertainty statements for a selected climate event.

tldr: Point-identified PN and PS are studied on separate rare factual-event shells. Fully specified abstract four-cell randomized profile tests have finite-experiment coverage, and a capped monotone submodel yields a shellwise lower diameter of order \(\min\{1,(nd)^{-1/2}\). On directional Gaussian sub-shells, cross-fitted score inversion has derived variance consistency, uniform coverage, and the matching shrinking upper rate. Continuous profile-LR construction and finite-profile transfer remain two explicit open questions.

project_justification.gap: Regular PN/PS inference does not calibrate shrinking factual probabilities, while rare-binomial and sample-size work does not provide learned-nuisance causal profiles or shellwise effective-count theory.
project_justification.niche: The proposal separates abstract discrete exactness, a derived continuous Gaussian score theorem, and the unresolved continuous likelihood-ratio bridge.
project_justification.fill: It supplies directional finite tests, marked-Poisson premises, primitive spline remainders, derived studentization, matching lower bounds, and two ordered continuous-LR questions.

related_work: Tian and Wu (2025) are the regular point-identified PN/PS comparator; their regular semiparametric inference does not establish rare-shell calibration or an \(nd\)-indexed diameter result. Cuellar and Kennedy (2020) give regular influence-function inference for a working-model projection of a conditional probability of causation, not this marginal monotone ratio or a rare factual-event shell. Zhang, Wang, and Miao (2025, arXiv:2504.08294v2) study generally partially identified PN bounds without monotonicity under a margin condition; that does not subsume a point-identified monotone PN/PS target on rare shells. Li, Mao, and Pearl (2022) determine sample sizes for specified PN/PS/PNS-bound accuracy, so the effective-count result explains why nominal total sample size is insufficient. Mikusheva and Sun (2022) study jackknife Anderson--Rubin inversion for many weak linear-IV instruments, not causal rare-cell profiling. Huwang (1995) motivates the normal-approximation failure and McGrath and Burke (2024) the rare-binomial coverage comparison. Hannart and Naveau (2018) and Kiriliouk and Naveau (2020) are climate consumers. No unverified primary-paper theorem, page, or equation anchor is asserted.
honest_scope: Finite-sample exactness is only for the abstract randomized product experiments. Marked-Poisson conclusions require every stated intensity, mark, and common-cell premise. Continuous score intervals have shrinking diameter only on their direction-specific Gaussian sub-shells. The continuous profile-LR procedure and finite-to-continuous transfer are open; no all-regime continuous upper frontier is claimed.
